In the first pair each item is replaced by its mirror partner across the middle of the pyramid: A with B, □ stays □, C with F, E with D. Doing the same: △ with ✱, D with E, ● with Ω, and ◬ (in the middle) stays. So the answer is ✱ E Ω ◬ (A).

Again each item is swapped with its mirror partner across the middle: △ with ✱, ⧅ with Ψ, ● with Ω, I with J, ◬ stays. Working back from JEF□◬: J with I, E with D, F with C, □ and ◬ stay. So the missing term is I D C □ ◬ (B).

Happy, glad and joyful all mean 'full of joy'. Cheerful means the same (D); rude, playful and merciful do not.

Each shape holds one circle fewer than twice its number of sides: pentagon \(2 \times 5 - 1 = 9\), square \(2 \times 4 - 1 = 7\), triangle \(2 \times 3 - 1 = 5\). The hexagon holds \(2 \times 6 - 1 = 11\) circles, so it fits (A). The octagon has 14 (needs 15), the seven-sided figure has 12 (needs 13), and a circle has no sides.

In the series A to Y, the 9th letter from the left is I, and the third letter to its left is F (6th). The 13th letter from the right is M, and the third letter to its right is P (16th). Midway between the 6th and 16th letters is the 11th, K (C).

For the fewest girls, Manasi stands in front of Vaishnavi. With 4 girls between them, Manasi is at \(22 - 5 = 17\)th from the front. She is also 17th from the back, so the queue has \(17 + 17 - 1 = 33\) girls (D). Placing Manasi behind Vaishnavi gives 43, which is larger.

Unfolding repeats the top-left quarter in all four quarters as mirror images. The small square at the centre corner becomes one large square in the middle (not a diamond or a flat rectangle, so not (1) or (2)), the quarter circles become half circles on the left and right edges, and the cut corner appears in all four corners. Figure (4) has only two black corners, so the answer is (3) (C).
